latin: मत्स्यांश्च खण्डशः कृत्वा चतुरङ्गुलसम्मितान् । लवणेन समायुक्तान् कुम्भेषु परिपूरयेत् ॥ ३३ ॥ खारखण्डा इति ख्याताश्चिरकालं वसन्ति ते । भोजनावसरे सूदो वह्निना परिभर्जयेत् ॥ ३४ ॥
english: And having cut fish into pieces measuring four fingerbreadths, and having mixed them with salt, he should pack them into jars. They are known as *khāra-khaṇḍas* [“salt-pieces”], and they keep for a long time. At mealtime the cook should roast them thoroughly over the fire. [The print reads *khāra-khaṇḍā*, p. 130; C and F read *khī-*.]

latin: मत्स्याण्डकोशावादाय वह्निना परिभर्जयेत् । दृढीभूते ततः पश्चात् खण्डशः परिकल्पयेत् ॥ ३५ ॥ विपच्य तप्ततैले तान्येलामरिचकादिभिः । विकीर्य सैन्धवेनापि हिङ्गुना परिधूपयेत् ॥ ३६ ॥
english: Having taken the two egg-sacs of the fish, he should roast them thoroughly over the fire. Then, once they have grown firm, he should afterwards cut them into pieces. Having cooked those pieces in hot oil, he should strew them with cardamom, pepper, and the like, and with rock salt as well, and should perfume them with asafoetida. [At 1535c the edition prints *dṛḍhībhūte* with the editor’s suggested dual *dṛḍhībhūtau*, agreeing with the two sacs, in parentheses, p. 130.]

latin: कच्छपान् वह्निना भृष्ट्वा पादांश्छल्कांश्च मोचयेत् । शिरश्चैव पृथक्कृत्वा पक्वरम्भाफलोपमान् ॥ ३७ ॥ अम्लकैश्च विपच्याथ तैलेनाज्येन वा पुनः । पाचयेच्च सुसिद्धांस्तान् चूर्णकैरवचूर्णयेत् ॥ ३८ ॥ आणके वा पचेत्तज्ज्ञो निधूमे वा हुताशने । नन्द्यावर्ता इति ख्याता मृदुरुच्या मनोहराः ॥ ३९ ॥
english: Having roasted turtles over the fire, he should work off the feet and the shell-plates, and separate the head as well — the turtles then resembling ripe plantain fruits. Then, having cooked them with sour things, he should cook them once more in oil, or else in ghee; and when they are thoroughly done he should dust them over with spice powders. Or one who knows the work may cook them in an *āṇaka* [a pan], or on a smokeless fire. They are known as *nandyāvartas*: of tender relish, delightful. [*pakvarambhāphalopamān* is accusative plural agreeing with *kacchapān*, the turtles themselves; there is no verb of cutting in the passage.]

latin: कर्कटांस्तु लघून्स्थूलान् हस्तपादवियोजितान् । रूक्षे ताम्रमये पात्रे सुतप्ते तान्विभर्जयेत् ॥ १५४० ॥ स्फोटिते खर्परे तांस्तु मृदो भाण्डे विनिक्षिपेत् । विपचेल्लवणाम्लैश्च पुनः सर्पिषि पाचयेत् ॥ ४१ ॥ जीरकं लवणं तीक्ष्णं चूर्णितं तेषु निक्षिपेत् । वृष्या बलकरा हृद्या मृष्टास्ते घृतकर्कटाः ॥ ४२ ॥
english: Crabs, whether small or large, with their claws and legs detached — he should roast them in a dry copper vessel, thoroughly heated. When the carapace has burst open, he should put them into a vessel of clay; he should cook them with salt and sour things, and then cook them again in ghee. He should throw powdered cumin, salt, and *tīkṣṇa* [a pungent spice] over them. These *ghṛta-karkaṭas* [“ghee-crabs”] are aphrodisiac, strength-giving, agreeable to the heart, and savoury. [1540d: the edition prints *tānvi(bha)varjayet*, p. 131, the parenthesis being the editor’s correction; *vibharjayet*, “he should roast them”, is the only reading that gives sense — the two scan identically, so the metre cannot decide it. 1541a: the print reads *kharpare*, a variant of *karpara*, here the crab’s shell, not a vessel — so the two vessels of the recipe are the dry copper pan and the earthen pot, and the switch comes exactly where the acid enters.]

latin: मूषकाः क्षेत्रसंभूता नदीकूलेषु संस्थिताः । स्थूलाः श्यामास्तथा पुष्टा जात्या ते मयिगाः स्मृताः ॥ ४३ ॥ प्रतप्ते सलिले तांस्तु निक्षिपेत्पुच्छधारणात् । उद्धृत्य तस्मात्सलिलाद्रोमाण्युत्पाटयेत्ततः ॥ ४४ ॥ विभेद्य जठरं तेषां स्फोटयेदन्त्रकाणि तु । सम्भारसहितैरम्लैः पचेच्च लवणान्वितैः ॥ ४५ ॥ शूलप्रोतांस्ततः कृत्वा तानङ्गारैः प्रतापयेत् । यावद्बहिस्त्वचस्तेषां शोषमायान्ति तापनात् ॥ ४६ ॥ सुपकेषु तथा तेषु मूषकेषु किरेदनु । लवणं मरिचं शुण्ठी जीरकं च विचूर्णितम् ॥ ४७ ॥
english: *Mūṣakas* [rats] are bred in the fields and settle along the banks of rivers; those that are large, dark, and well-fed are, by their kind, called *mayigas*. He should drop them into thoroughly heated water, holding each by the tail; and lifting it out of that water, he should then pluck out the hairs. Splitting open their belly, he should burst out the entrails; and he should cook them with sour things furnished with seasonings and joined with salt. Then, having got them pierced on a skewer, he should heat them over coals, until their outer skins go dry from the heating. And when those *mūṣakas* are well cooked, he should afterwards scatter over them salt, pepper, dried ginger, and cumin, all powdered. [1543a and 1547b: the edition prints *mūkha(ṣa)kāḥ* and *mūkha(ṣa)keṣu*, p. 131, the parenthesis being the editor’s correction to *mūṣaka*. 1544 has *salila*, water — not oil. The skin is not removed: only the hairs are pulled out, and 1546 makes the drying of the outer skin the test of doneness. 1547a: the print reads *supakeṣu* for the expected *supakveṣu*; 1547d *śuṇṭhī* for the expected accusative *śuṇṭhīm*.]

latin: फलशाकं पत्रशाकं कन्दशाकं च मूलकम् । पुष्पशाकं शिम्बिशाकं पक्वापक्वविभेदतः ॥ ४८ ॥ कल्पयेद्द्विविधैः शाकैर्मांसवत् पाककोविदः । वटकान् पर्पटान् हृद्यानङ्गारैः परिभर्जयेत् ॥ ४९ ॥
english: Fruit-vegetable, leaf-vegetable, tuber-vegetable, and root; flower-vegetable and pod-vegetable — each according to the distinction of ripe and unripe. With vegetables of the two kinds the cook expert in cooking should prepare dishes just as with meat; and *vaṭakas* and *parpaṭas*, which are agreeable, he should roast thoroughly over coals. [1549a: the print reads *kalpayed dvividhaiḥ*, p. 132, “of the two kinds”, which picks up the ripe/unripe distinction of 1548d — not *vividhaiḥ*, “various”.]

latin: आम्राम्रातकजम्बूश्च बीजपूराग्निमन्थकैः । भल्लातागस्त्यकोपासिद्राक्षाभृङ्गकसल्लकैः ॥ ५० ॥ पुनर्नवा मरी तीक्ष्णा अतसी सुरसाद्वयम् । मरुकं तालपर्णी च भिण्डुकी मुण्डका तथा ॥ ५१ ॥ ब्राह्मी चैवाम्लपत्री च कोकिलाक्षी कुसुम्भकम् । अञ्जनं पद्मकोशश्च शेढकं च तथापरम् ॥ ५२ ॥ सङ्गृह्य पल्लवानेषामम्लिकाम्लेन मिश्रयेत् । जम्बीराम्लेन दध्ना वा लवणेन च संयुतान् ॥ ५३ ॥
english: With mango, hog plum, and *jambū*; with citron and *agnimantha*; with *bhallāta*, *agastya*, *kopāsi*, grape, *bhṛṅgaka*, and *sallaka*; *punarnavā*, *marī*, *tīkṣṇā*, flax, and the two *surasās*; *maruka* and *tālaparṇī*, and *bhiṇḍukī* and *muṇḍakā* likewise; and *brāhmī*, and sour-leaf, and *kokilākṣī*, and safflower; *añjana*, and the lotus-calyx, and *śeḍhaka*, and yet another besides — having gathered the tender shoots of these, he should mix them with the sourness of tamarind, or with the sourness of lime, or with curd, and joined with salt as well. [1550c: the print reads *kopāsi*, p. 132 — unidentified, and the metrical cadence requires the long *-pā-*. 1553a: the edition prints *amla(mli)kāmlena*, the parenthesis being the editor’s correction to *amlikā*, tamarind.]

latin: श्रीफलं केतकं चिञ्चा मेषशृङ्गी सुगन्धिजम् । कुटजं मरिचं पथ्या विषमुष्टिकशिम्बिजम् ॥ ५४ ॥ एलारामठनीवारमेथिकापर्पटं तथा । अगस्त्यं नन्दनं राजमातुलिङ्गकपाटलिं ॥ ५५ ॥ कटं मटं कर्कटं च करीरं टेण्टुकं तथा । वेत्रकारीफलं चैव लवणाम्भासि निक्षिपेत् ॥ ५६ ॥ चूतमाम्रातकं धात्री कुहिरी कर्कटी तथा । कूष्माण्डं त्रपुसं द्राक्षा कर्कटी बृहतीद्वयम् ॥ ५७ ॥ कोशातकीबीजपूरं निष्पावं करमर्दकम् । जम्बीरबिम्बवार्ताककर्मरं लवणाम्भासि ॥ ५८ ॥
english: Bael, *ketaka* [screw pine], tamarind, *meṣaśṛṅgī*, *sugandhija*; *kuṭaja*, pepper, *pathyā* [chebulic myrobalan], and what comes of the pod of *viṣamuṣṭika*; cardamom, asafoetida, *nīvāra* [wild rice], fenugreek, and *parpaṭa* likewise; *agastya*, *nandana*, royal citron, and *pāṭali* — *kaṭa*, *maṭa*, and *karkaṭa*, and *karīra* and *ṭeṇṭuka* likewise, and cane and *kārīphala*: he should put these into salt water. Mango, hog plum, *dhātrī* [emblic myrobalan], *kuhirī*, and *karkaṭī* likewise; ash gourd, cucumber, grapes, *karkaṭī*, the two *bṛhatīs*; *kośātakī* [ridge gourd], citron, *niṣpāva* [lablab bean, its pods eaten whole], *karamardaka*; lime, ivy gourd, eggplant, and *karmara* — into salt water. [1555d: the print reads *-kapāṭaliṃ*, p. 132, accusative of the feminine *pāṭali*, the trumpet-flower; D reads *-liḥ*. Our *pāṭālam* broke the cadence. 1556a: the print reads *maṭaṃ*, not *madaṃ*. 1557: *karkaṭī* stands twice in the printed verse, in b and in d. 1556d and 1558d: the print reads *lavaṇāmbhāsi* in both places, where the expected locative singular is *lavaṇāmbhasi*.]

latin: अथवा राजिकाचूर्णे सतैले लवणान्विते । प्रक्षाल्य वृन्तसहितं फलं चूतादिकं न्यसेत् ॥ ५९ ॥ कारवेल्लं सपनसं कदलीफलमेव च । सतैले राजिकाचूर्णे निक्षिपेल्लवणान्विते ॥ १५६० ॥
english: Or else: in powdered mustard mixed with oil and joined with salt, having washed it, he should set down the fruit together with its stalk — mango and the like. Bitter gourd, along with jackfruit, and banana fruit as well, he should put into powdered mustard mixed with oil and joined with salt.

latin: वंशाङ्कुरं लघुं चक्रीं शतावर्यास्तथैव च । पातालटेण्टुकानां च प्ररोहान्क्षालितान्मृदून् ॥ ६१ ॥ सलिले लवणोपेते तैले वाऽपि सराजिके । लवणेन समायुक्ते प्रक्षिपेदङ्कुरानिमान् ॥ ६२ ॥ मागिणीमार्द्रकं पैष्टुं कचोरं वनमागिणीम् । कर्पूरमागिणीमूलं तथैवाम्लहरिद्रका ॥ ६३ ॥ सूरणं मधुशिग्रुं च तथा शंबलकन्दकम् । एतानि पूर्ववत्कृत्वा तैले वापि विनिक्षिपेत् ॥ ६४ ॥
english: Bamboo shoot, the small *cakrī*, and likewise the shoots of *śatāvarī*, and the sprouts of the *pātāla-ṭeṇṭukas*, washed and tender — into water furnished with salt, or else into oil with mustard and joined with salt, he should throw these sprouts. *Māgiṇī* and fresh ginger, *paiṣṭu*, *kacora* [zedoary], and wild *māgiṇī*; the root of camphor-*māgiṇī*, and likewise sour turmeric [*amla-haridrakā*, mango ginger]; elephant-foot yam and sweet *śigru* [a variety of the drumstick tree], and likewise the *śaṃbala*-bulb — having prepared these as before, he should put them into oil as well. [1561a: the print reads *laghuṃ*, p. 133, which the cadence requires. 1563a: the print reads *māgiṇīmārdrakaṃ*, i.e. *māgiṇīm* + *ārdrakaṃ*, fresh ginger; our *māgiṇīmākaṃ* was a syllable short. 1563d: the print reads *haridrakā*, not *-kām*. 1564: the print reads *madhuśigruṃ* and *śaṃbalakandakam*; our *bilakandakam* was a syllable short, and D reads *vaṣṭha-*.]
